plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like blooms in autumn without any leaves present. The foliage emerges the following spring, then dies back by early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September–October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to meadows of Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America, the UK, and Australia
plants.funFact: All parts contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall, rhizomatous perennial with arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators preparing for winter or migration.
plants.location: Native to meadows, roadsides, and prairies of North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Despite its reputation, goldenrod is rarely the cause of hay fever; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time but has wind-borne pollen.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A bulbous perennial whose leafless stalks suddenly erupt in clusters of striking red flowers with long, curved stamens. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering and persist through winter.
plants.location: Native to China, Korea, and Japan; naturalized in the southeastern United States; commonly seen along rice paddies and cemeteries in Japan
plants.funFact: In Japan it blooms around the autumn equinox (Higan) and is called higanbana; it is often planted around rice fields because the toxic bulbs deter rodents and moles.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A large evergreen shrub producing the biggest flower heads in the Protea genus, made of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It thrives in nutrient-poor, acidic, well-drained soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August–November, peaking around September)
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its fire-adapted woody rootstock allows it to resprout after wildfires.
